guidance: If the reading runs lines together differently from the print, or puts a few words at the edge of the box in another order, that still counts as Yes.
If the reading has the block's text and more besides (words from the next column), answer Yes.
If the box holds no text at all (a picture, an ornament, a rule or blank paper), pick Not text. A headline or an advertisement is text.
intro: A program read each of these English-language newspaper pages from Chronicling America, the Library of Congress's collection of historic American newspapers. We want to know whether it missed any of the print.
name: English: missing text
question: Does the machine reading include all the words printed in the box? Ignore spelling mistakes and a word or two cut off at the edge of the box: answer No only if a line or more is missing.
rules: The box marks a block of print, shown enlarged below it, with the machine reading of the same place under that. Spelling doesn't count here. Answer No if a line or more of the print in the box (a line, a passage, a column) is missing from the reading, even if the rest is perfect.
title: English newspapers: missing text
